title: Gas-phase oxidation of myrtenal: temperature-dependent kinetics and gas-phase products from NO 3 -initiated reactions in atmospheric simulation chambers
content: The gas-phase reactions of first-generation terpene oxidation products (FGTOPs) play an important role in atmospheric chemistry by influencing air quality, climate, and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. Despite their atmospheric relevance, the kinetics and oxidation mechanisms of FGTOPs, such as myrtenal, remain poorly characterized. In this study, we investigated the reaction of myrtenal with NO3 radicals in four atmospheric simulation chambers (THALAMOS, CHARME, IASC, and ESC-Q-UAIC), enabling comparison and cross-validation of kinetic and mechanistic measurements and the identification of gas-phase oxidation products. The rate coefficient at (295 ± 3) K and atmospheric pressure was determined using the relative-rate (RR) method to be k(myrtenal+NO3) = (2.44 ± 0.34) × 10−14 cm3 molecule−1 s−1. Furthermore, the temperature-dependent rate coefficient was evaluated using the RR method over the temperature range 293–353 K, resulting in the following Arrhenius expression: Alt-text is not available for this image.. The results reveal that the reaction follows weak positive temperature dependence over 293–353 K. Using this rate coefficient, we determined the atmospheric lifetime of myrtenal with respect to NO3 to be ∼57 hours at nighttime and ∼47 days during daytime, using typical NO3 concentrations of 2 × 108 molecules cm−3 and 1 × 107 molecules cm−3, respectively. Gas-phase oxidation products were characterized using complementary analytical techniques, including PTR-ToF-MS, TD-GC-EI-MS, and ToF-CIMS. Acetone and a range of oxygenated products were identified, including an unsaturated ketone, norinone, epoxides, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids, organic nitrates (ONs) and nitrooxy ketones. Based on the identified products, a degradation mechanism involving both NO3 addition and H-atom abstraction pathways is proposed.
